messages:
Raj: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — collecting concrete questions about the runtime perf / batching / kernel work. I'll try to answer or route to owners.

Elaine: thanks! first: what's the rollout cadence for the new attention kernel? are we doing small canaries or big waves?

Raj: small staged canaries. target: 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h/48h hold windows depending on perf signals. aim is conservative for LLMs.

Sam: what are the precise perf signals that will block a rollout? latency p99 delta? error rate? cost regressions?

Raj: primary blockers: p50/p95/p99 regressions beyond SLO delta, token error rate (>=2x baseline), and any increase in tail GC or OOMs. cost increase is a factor but we won't block purely for a small cost bump if latency improves.

Julie: for batching/cache interactions, do we plan to change default cache TTLs or expose smarter cache invalidation? request patterns vary a lot across tenants.

Elaine: we prototyped adaptive TTL in dev: TTL adapts to prefix-hit rate per route. Default remains 30s, opt-in per route. roadmap item: make adaptive TTL GA after a month of production signals.

Morgan: will customers need to change SDK / prompting to get benefits? any breaking changes?

Elaine: no breaking changes. most gains are runtime-side. we'll add an opt-in route flag: "use_adaptive_cache": true and a thin migration doc.

Sam: can we have a dashboard tile for canary rollouts that shows p50/p95/p99 + mem pressure + KV cache hit-rate? ops needs one-click abort.

Raj: yes — console card is planned. initial version shows p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, and kv hit-rate. abort and rollback buttons will wire to the rollout controller.

Julie: regarding kernel work: are we keeping a single monolithic kernel per model or per-opaque-variant (quantization, seq-len optimized)?

Elaine: per-variant. kernel selection logic will map model artifact + quantization profile + seq-length bucket -> kernel. we cache the mapping in the node agent.

Morgan: curious about telemetry — what traces/logs should engineering customers expect if they opt into dedicated?

Raj: we'll expose per-token latency breakdowns (kernel execution, kv lookup, batching wait), batch size distribution histograms, and a kernel-selection trace. GDPR-safe, no raw prompts logged unless customer enables eval logging.

Sam: can you paste the canary config snippet we'll use (so SRE can add monitors)?

Elaine: sure — example yaml:```\ncanary:\n  steps:\n    - pct: 2\n      hold: 24h\n    - pct: 10\n      hold: 24h\n    - pct: 50\n      hold: 48h\nsignals:\n  latency:\n    p95_increase_threshold: 1.15\n  errors:\n    rate_multiplier: 2.0\n  kv:\n    hit_rate_drop: 0.2\n```\n
Sam: perfect, will add monitors and an automated rollback playbook.

Morgan: can we get a short migration note in the release notes about adaptive TTL + kernel selection behavior? one-liner for customers + link to deep doc.

Raj: yes — Morgan and Elaine will draft a 3-bullet release note. Elaine, can you own the deep doc?

Elaine: will do. target first draft by EOD Friday.

OpsBot: Deploy bot: canary-controller/rollout-job started for experiment/attention-kernel-v2 at 1776544005 :rocket:

Sam: saw the bot — I'll watch the monitors and ping here if anything spikes. :eyes:

Raj: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short summary for the release thread and link to the deep doc once ready.
